target.title: refactor(msteams): remove obsolete sso invoke stack
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

MSTeams retained a custom SSO invoke implementation after the Teams SDK became the runtime owner for `signin/tokenExchange` and `signin/verifyState`. The old helpers, handler dependency, tests, and exports had no production callers but still duplicated the SDK contract.

## Why This Change Was Made

- Remove the unwired custom SSO invoke stack and its handler-only tests.
- Keep the active SDK SSO path unchanged through `oauthDefaultConnectionName`, `onTokenExchange`, and `onVerifyState`.
- Remove second-order dead exports exposed by the deletion.
- Drop the obsolete MSTeams entries from the dead-export baseline.

## User Impact

No user-visible behavior or configuration changes. MSTeams SSO continues to use the Teams SDK routes and the existing token persistence callbacks.

## Evidence

- Codebase graph and repository search found no production callers for the removed invoke helpers.
- Direct inspection of `@microsoft/teams.apps` 2.0.13 confirmed the SDK owns both signin routes and their token exchange / verify-state semantics.
- Fresh Testbox focused suite: 4 files, 38 tests passed.
- Fresh `gpt-5.6-sol` medium autoreview: no findings, patch correct at 0.87 confidence.
- Reviewed staged tree and committed tree both resolve to `3f6941d12bcbfc3576fb513b266d86fb0ced47d0`.
- `git diff --check` passes.
- Net production/test/tooling reduction: 17 additions, 525 deletions.

No changelog entry: this is an internal dead-code refactor with unchanged runtime behavior.
